Welcome to
Sarum Academy
Welcome to Sarum Academy! Rooted in the rich values and traditions of the Church of England, our vibrant and inclusive school aims to inspire everyone to pursue ambitious goals, lead lives of purpose and make a lasting impact on society.
We offer a wide-ranging curriculum alongside a nurturing community where individuality is celebrated.
Our values of respect, ambition, and excellence drive everything we do, preparing students to thrive both personally and academically. Whether you are a prospective student, parent, or a member of our wider community, we are delighted you are exploring what makes Sarum Academy so special.
Come and see what makes Sarum Academy unique. We’d love to welcome you to our community.
Our Updates
🎃🍂 HAPPY HALF TERM! 🍂🎃 What a fantastic Term 1 we have had! We would like to say a huge thank you to all our students, families and staff for their hard work, commitment and support this term. We look forward to welcoming you back after half term on Monday 2nd November Wishing all our students and families a happy, safe and spook-tacular half-term break! 🎃🍁
We love seeing and supporting our local Primary schools Fantastic learning and behaviour Pembroke!
Year 8 Football A strong second-half performance saw our Year 8's secure a hard-fought 2-0 victory over Trafalgar in a closely contested encounter. The first half was evenly matched, with both sides battling hard and neither team able to break the deadlock. Defences remained on top and chances were limited, resulting in a goalless scoreline at the interval. The introductions made at half-time injected fresh energy into the Sarum attack, and the breakthrough soon followed. Some excellent combination play between Max and Mason earned Sarum a corner. When the ball was delivered into the box, it fell kindly to Jensen, who showed great composure to calmly tap home from close range and give Sarum the lead. Buoyed by the goal, Sarum continued to press high and attack the heart of the Trafalgar defence. Quin was a constant threat, testing the visitors with his direct running and creating problems throughout the second half. As Sarum pushed for a second goal, the pressure continued to build. Another corner caused chaos in the penalty area, and after a handball was spotted on the line, the referee pointed to the penalty spot. Up stepped Oli, who confidently dispatched the penalty with just five minutes remaining to put the result beyond doubt. Despite the two-goal deficit, Trafalgar refused to give in and continued to battle until the final whistle, creating a few anxious moments as they pushed forward in search of a way back into the game. Full Time: Sarum Academy 2–0 Trafalgar A massive thank you to Trafalgar for being excellent opponents throughout, showing great determination and sportsmanship from start to finish. We wish them the very best of luck for the remainder of the season. Special recognition also goes to Jack, Arlo, Leighton and Harrison for their support with officiating, and to Riley for his assistance in the dugout. Finally, thank you to all the students, parents and supporters who came out to watch and cheer on the team.
🌺 The Poppy Appeal – Supporting Our Armed Forces Community The reception/admin office has this year's Poppy Appeal items available, with a selection of poppies, themed items and accessories. The Royal British Legion's Poppy Appeal raises vital funds to support serving and ex-serving members of the Armed Forces, veterans and their families when they need help. Please pop into the office to have a look if you would like to purchase anything. A small cash donation of at least £1 per item is requested. Every donation, no matter how small, helps make a difference. Thank you for your support!
Our talented students have officially submitted their entries for the national Harvest Festival Wheatsheaf Loaf Challenge! 🥖 We had 4 fantastic groups of students take part this year, showing off some serious baking skills and incredible creativity. 🎨👩🍳👨🍳 A massive, heartfelt thank you goes to the amazing Jenny Brown from our school canteen team. Your guidance, support, and endless encouragement made this whole challenge possiblewe couldn't have done it without you! 🙌 Fingers crossed for the £500 kitchen equipment prize! 🤞🏆 Good luck to everyone who took part! We are so proud of you all. 🌟
Look who is coming for lunch tomorrow!!
What a joy it was to spend yesterday afternoon with this fabulous bunch... even if you did manage to beat Miss Gough at bowling! 🎳 15 students from Years 8 and 9 were selected to enjoy our first rewards trip of the year, recognising their brilliant conduct, excellent attendance and fantastic improvements in behaviour. We are SO proud of you all! What a fantastic way to kick-start the year! Keep your eyes peeled for our next rewards trip just before Christmas... 🎄👀 I wonder where we'll be heading next!
Year 10 Football Match Report: Sarum Academy 1–0 Trafalgar School A hard-fought victory for Sarum! Sarum Academy's Year 10 football team secured a narrow 1–0 victory over Trafalgar School in a closely contested fixture. In truth, the game felt like a draw, with both teams cancelling each other out for large periods and creating a competitive, evenly matched encounter. The decisive moment came through some excellent pressing from Eroni, whose intensity forced the Trafalgar defence and goalkeeper into an error. Eroni was on hand to capitalise and finish comfortably, giving Sarum the only goal of the game and ultimately securing the win. There were several notable performances across the team. George and Alex were as solid as ever at the back, providing a dependable defensive foundation. Henry also proved to be an excellent outlet on the right-hand side, combining direct running with relentless energy throughout the match. However, Jake takes the Man of the Match award for another impressive performance this season. His composure on the ball continues to stand out, particularly when operating in tight defensive areas under pressure. His ability to remain calm and make good decisions in difficult situations was a real positive and a key feature of his performance. The game also provided a valuable opportunity to experiment tactically, with several players taking on slightly different roles and positions as we explored alternative formations. This flexibility will be important as the season progresses. Well done to John, who stepped up to play a year above his age group and contributed to the squad. A big thank you to our Year 11 students, Jack, Marley and Leighton, for running the lines and refereeing the game. Their support was greatly appreciated. We would also like to thank Trafalgar School for making the journey to play the fixture. Finally, a huge thank you to the fantastic support from the students and parents who came along to watch the game. Your encouragement from the sidelines was greatly appreciated by the team and helped make it a great occasion. Well done to the Year 10 boys on the victory! It was a competitive game that could have gone either way, but the team showed the determination needed to come away with the result. Hopefully, this is the first of many local league victories this season! Mr Lawrence

Headteacher's Welcome
It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to Sarum Academy. Rooted in the values and traditions of the Church of England, our academy is a vibrant, inclusive, and nurturing community where every individual is valued and supported to achieve their full potential. Whether you are a prospective student, parent, or a member of our wider community, I am delighted you are exploring what makes Sarum Academy so special.
At Sarum Academy, we are inspired by the Church of England's vision for education: to provide a foundation for wisdom, hope, community, and dignity. These guiding principles, woven into our ethos, ensure that all we do is centred on creating an environment where each person can flourish in body, mind, and spirit.
Our core values—Respect, Ambition, and Excellence—reflect this vision.
Respect is at the heart of our community. We believe every individual is created in the image of God and has inherent worth and dignity. By fostering mutual respect, we create a safe and inclusive environment where diversity is celebrated, and kindness and understanding are central to how we treat one another.
Ambition speaks to our belief in the boundless potential of every child. We strive to nurture a spirit of hope and resilience, encouraging students to aim high and embrace challenges with courage and determination. In doing so, we equip them to contribute meaningfully to the world and fulfil their unique God-given talents.
Excellence reflects our commitment to delivering a rich and transformative education. Through high standards and a focus on lifelong learning, we inspire our students to achieve their best academically while growing spiritually and morally. Excellence at Sarum Academy is not just about personal success but also about living out values of service, generosity, and love for others.
Our staff are dedicated to fostering a sense of belonging, joy, and purpose for every student, ensuring that they are supported holistically—academically, emotionally, and spiritually. We are proud to offer a curriculum enriched by opportunities for creativity, exploration, and reflection, alongside a strong pastoral system that nurtures wellbeing and character development.
As a Church of England Academy, we encourage students to explore life’s deeper questions, develop moral courage, and grow in faith. Together, we seek to shape individuals who embody wisdom, compassion, and hope, making a positive difference in the world around them.
We warmly invite you to visit us and experience the spirit of Sarum Academy for yourself. Please explore our website to learn more, or better still, come and meet us in person. We look forward to welcoming you into the Sarum Academy family, where every member is cherished and supported to thrive.

Attendance - Information for Parents
Why Attendance Matters
Regular school attendance is essential for children to make the most of their education. By attending school daily, children can achieve their full potential, build strong relationships, and develop good habits for the future. Our school deems 97% as the benchmark for good attendance as it accepts that some level of absence due to illness may be unavoidable but is certainly not inevitable.
Our Attendance Champion is: Rebecca Brosnan
Contact details: rebecca.brosnan@sarumacademy.org
Our Attendance Officer is: Kayleigh Harvey
Contact details: kayleigh.harvey@sarumacademy.org
Reporting an Absence
Before you report an absence, are you aware of your child's attendance?
If your child is going to be absent, please contact the school as soon as possible. The phone is staffed from 8.00am. You can reach our Attendance Office by:
Email: enquiries@sarumacademy.org
Please provide your child's name, class, reason for absence, and expected return date. You are expected to call in and report absence everyday your child is absent. We will be in contact if we have not heard from you.
There is no entitlement in law to time off in term time. Magna Learning Partnership Academies will not authorise leave of absence in term time unless there are exceptional circumstances. Whilst there is not a definitive list of circumstances these are typically for the following reasons:
Unavoidable medical or dental appointments
Close immediate family bereavement
For religious observance
Gypsy Roma Traveller absence when the family is travelling for occupational purposes only
Matters relating to a child’s welfare
All holiday is unauthorised regardless of the reason. Individual cases will be addressed by the Academy Leader, there decision is final.
Download an Absence Request Form - Microsoft Word Version, PDF Version
Authorised vs. Unauthorised Absence
Understanding the difference between authorised and unauthorised absences is important for maintaining good attendance records.
Authorised Absences: These are absences that the school may approve. Examples include:
Illness: If your child is too sick to attend school.
Medical/Dental Appointments: If these cannot be scheduled outside school hours.
Family Emergencies: Such as a bereavement or other significant events.
Religious Observances: When observance falls on a school day.
To have an absence authorised, please provide details explaining the reason. For medical absences, a doctor’s note may be required for prolonged or frequent absences. Remember an absence may be authorised but it still counts against your child’s attendance record.
Unauthorised Absences: These are absences that the school will not approve. Examples include:
Unexplained Absences: Not providing a reason for the absence.
Holidays: Taking vacations during term time.
Shopping Trips: Going shopping during school hours.
Lack of uniform: Your child being absent as their uniform is in the wash
Transport difficulties: Your child being absent as they have missed the bus
Non-Urgent Appointments: Such as haircuts, beauty treatments, or driving lessons.
Family events: Day trips, weddings, or visiting relatives.
Unauthorised absences can impact a child’s learning and overall attendance record. If you are unsure whether an absence will be authorised, please contact the Attendance Office.
Importance of Punctuality
Being on time is equally important. Arriving late can disrupt the class and affect your child’s learning. If your child is late, please ensure they check in at the school office upon arrival.
What to do if your child is ill?
When assessing whether to send your child to school or not, consider whether an adult would take a day off from work in a similar situation. If they are too unwell to attend school, please do keep them at home, but if they feel able to attend we have a medical facility and a medical officer should symptoms get worse during the day.
For sickness or diarrhoea, the school’s policy is for a child to be off for 48 hours.
You do not need to keep your child home from school if they have:
Athlete’s foot, Cold Sores, Conjunctivitis, Glandular Fever, Head Lice, Tonsillitis, Cold or Cough, Headaches, Sore Throat.
The NHS gives the following advice on how long children should stay off school if they are unwell. https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/is-my-child-too-ill-for-school/
Support for Attendance Issues
We understand that there can be challenges in maintaining regular attendance. Our school is committed to working with parents to address these issues. Here’s how we can help:
Regular Communication: We will keep you informed about your child's attendance record and address any concerns promptly.
Attendance Meetings: We can schedule meetings to discuss any issues affecting your child’s attendance and work together to find solutions.
Resources and Referrals: We can provide resources or refer you to external support services if needed.
Personalised Support Plans: For children with chronic attendance issues, we can develop a support plan tailored to their specific needs.
We have developed a five stage supportive attendance process to support our young people in improving their attendance.
Pre-Stage 1 your child’s tutor may contact you if they have any worries
Stage 1 is letting you know we have some concerns
Stage 2 will let you know if attendance is not improving and try and find out the reasons why
Stage 3 will be a supportive school attendance meeting with a plan set and agreed
Stage 4 will be a review of the plan
Stage 5 will be a referral to the Educational Welfare Service
If you are experiencing difficulties with ensuring your child’s regular attendance, please contact us. Our team is here to help and can provide support and resources to address any challenges.
For more information please contact us:
Attendance Officer: Kayleigh Harvey
Email: kayleigh.harvey@sarumacademy.org
Let’s work together to ensure every child attends school regularly and on time, ready to learn and succeed!

Year Six Transition
We are very much looking forward to welcoming you and your family to the Academy community and we will keep you updated via the website.
We appreciate that a successful transition depends on a range of things such as supporting students in building positive relationships with their teachers and tutor group, creating the right environment where students feel safe and secure and for us as an Academy to successfully work in partnership with parents and carers. We are working collaboratively with the primary schools to ensure that we have all of the relevant information needed to best support your child when they join us.
It is often parents and carers that worry the most and this could be because you are unsure of what to expect but you want to offer your child reassurance and support but don’t necessarily have the information to do so. There are lots of people at the Academy who can support your child through the transition process and we know that they are likely to feel anxious or nervous but this perfectly normal.
If you have any specific queries or concerns that you would like to discuss, please don’t hesitate to email us at transition@sarumacademy.org

Y7 - 9 Curriculum (KS3)
The Key Stage 3 curriculum covers years 7, 8 and 9. Students follow a curriculum in the following subjects in English Language, English Literature, Mathematics, Science, Religious Studies, Physical Education and PSHCE, all of which will continue as a core offer into Key stage 4. The timetable covers 50 hours across a two-week timetable. Students will be taught in these core subjects for 29 out of the 50 hours. In addition, students follow a broad curriculum as they are taught Art, Food Technology, Geography, History, IT, Music and Modern Foreign Languages.
Core Subjects
Science – Double Award
Optional Subjects
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) In Year 7, each child is given a main language to study (either French or Spanish), which they learn for 3 hours per fortnight. They also have 1 hour of the other language, plus 1 hour of German, giving them a broad introduction to language learning.
In Year 8, students have 3 hours of French and 2 hours of Spanish.
In Year 9, their focus is on French, with 4 hours per fortnight.
Maths, English and Science To make sure students are well prepared for the demands of the curriculum, students now receive:
8 hours of Maths per fortnight
7 hours of English per fortnight
7 hours of Science, rising to 8 hours in Year 9
This allows us to cover the curriculum in greater depth and support strong progress in these core subjects.
Information Technology (IT) IT is taught throughout all of KS3.
In Year 7, students have 1 hour per fortnight.
In Years 8 and 9, IT is taught through a carousel with Food Technology, giving students a balance of digital and practical skills.
We are aiming to increase IT teaching time in the future as digital skills become increasingly important.
